relations.note: He is Aino’s brother in Lönnrot’s composite and canonical genealogy.
After losing the singing contest, he promises Aino to Väinämöinen without consulting her.

relations.myth: Aino is offered as Väinämöinen’s wife
relations.note: He accepts Joukahainen’s offer of Aino, but the proposed marriage never occurs.
He demands that Aino adorn herself for him; she rejects him and flees.
He catches but fails to recognize and retain Aino’s posthumous aquatic form.
Aino wears gold ornaments Kuutar had previously given to her mother.
Aino wears silver ornaments Päivätär had previously supplied to her mother.

relations.myth: Aino enters the realm of Vellamo’s maidens
relations.note: Aino’s fish-form appears in Vellamo’s aquatic domain, though Aino is not Vellamo.

relations.myth: Aino’s fish-form appears in Ahto’s realm
relations.note: Her aquatic form is caught after Väinämöinen seeks Ahto’s underwater realm.
Source criticism identifies Anni as a major oral antecedent of Lönnrot’s composite Aino.

relations.myth: Caught water maiden becomes posthumous Aino
relations.note: Lönnrot identifies the independently attested caught water maiden with Aino’s fish-form.

relations.myth: Osmoinen approaches Anni in the forest
relations.note: This unwelcome suitor confronts Anni, an oral antecedent later incorporated into Aino.

relations.myth: Kalevainen approaches Anni in the forest
relations.note: In regional variants he is Anni’s unwelcome suitor, a role transferred into Aino’s story.
